note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation in this book was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS New Testament wording and the 1962-register Old Testament renderings the first translation carried.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse, verses joined, the shortest contiguous span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'; a verbatim recitation without quote marks counts (founder rule, 2026-11-19). `self_rendered` rows each carry a `why`: allusions woven into Brengle's prose, his summaries of Bible lives, the seeker's own words, and two hymn quotations (Charles Wesley) that echo a verse without quoting it.

Judgement calls: 'Pure in Heart' (Matt 5:8) is OWB's «ልባቸው ንጹሕ የሆነ» wherever the beatitude is quoted, and 'blessed' its «የተባረኩ»; the book's running term «ንጹሕ ልብ» stays in the prose. 'He was without sin' is OWB Heb 4:15 «ነገር ግን ኃጢአት አልሠራም»; 'The Man of Sorrows' is OWB Isa 53:3 «የሥቃይ ሰው»; 'in heaviness through manifold temptations' (which Brengle gives to Paul; it is 1 Pet 1:6) quotes OWB's «በልዩ ልዩ ፈተናዎች» with the prose carrying the heaviness. The sow 'washed … wallowing in the mire' is OWB 2 Pet 2:22 «አሳማ ከታጠበ በኋላ በጭቃ ወደ መንከባለል ይመለሳል». 'Not that we loved God, but that He loved us' joins two OWB pieces of 1 John 4:10. 'Enoch walked with God three hundred years' is OWB Gen 5:22 «ሄኖክ 300 ዓመት ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ተመላለሰ» (am.json decision `walked-with-god`). 'What must I do to be pure?' (ch. 7) is the reader's question, not Acts 22:10, and stays the translator's. The hymn line 'All things are possible to him / That can in Jesus' name believe' is not Mark 9:23 and is not forced to the `all-things-possible` refrain.
